_comment: OpenBot action policy (AGENT_COMPUTER_POLICY). Evaluated by the gateway
BEFORE every browser / file / shell / MCP action. Deny rules are evaluated
before allow rules, and missing or malformed policy FAILS CLOSED.
IMPORTANT: the policy that ships in OpenBot's start script allows all
actions. That is fine for a laptop demo and unacceptable for a bot that
spends money and publishes to a live storefront. Replace it with this.
Rules are CEL expressions. Available fields include tool name, intent,
bot id, page url, element attributes and file path. Consult
OpenBot docs/policy.md for the exact schema of your pinned version --
field names have moved between alpha releases, so verify against the
commit you deploy rather than trusting this file blindly.

deny.why: A bot that can edit billing can drain the account. Fulfillment billing is set once by a human and never touched again.
Same. Printful billing methods are a human-only surface.
Disconnecting the store breaks fulfillment for every open order.
'Manually confirm imported orders' and shipping profiles must stay exactly as a human set them. A bot flipping one of these silently stops all fulfillment.
Token and webhook config is infrastructure. Changing it breaks attribution.
Hard ceiling. The Sentinel checks budget too; this is the second, independent layer. Two layers because one layer is a rounding error away from a bad month.
Irreversible destruction of records you legally must keep.
Prompt injection arrives as a web page. A research bot that follows a link into an attacker's page can be told to do anything. Confining navigation to a fixed allowlist is the containment.
Shell is the escape hatch from every other rule. Restrict it to the pipeline entrypoints.
Keep artifacts inside the bot's own container volume.
Secrets are injected as env vars and must never be read back into a transcript or a file the model can see.

allow.why: THE reason this bot needs a browser at all. ecom_visibility is read-only in the Square API; flipping Site visibility to Visible for a new Printful item is a dashboard-only action.
Ground truth for 'is this actually purchasable'. Reads the public site, clicks nothing.
NEEDS_APPROVAL orders are paid-but-unprinted. A human should normally handle these; allow read + the single 'Complete order' action so the bot can unstick a known-benign case and alarm on the rest.
Demand discovery requires real pages. Google Trends, Etsy search, Amazon BSR, Reddit, Pinterest.
IP screening must reach the authoritative registry.
The bots invoke the Python pipeline. Only the pod.* entrypoints are reachable.
Design artifacts, reports, cached signal data.
